articles.title: GPT-6 Astra
articles.content:
GPT

Astra

Update on September 29, 2026:Learn about OpenAI's latest model:GPT‑6 .1 Sol⁠.

Update on September 22, 2026:We are expanding our GPT‑6 family with GPT‑6 Sol and GPT‑6 Luna.Learn more.

We’re introducing GPT‑6 Astra, the world’s most intelligent and aligned model.

GPT‑6 Astra brings together years of research and big bets across pre-training, reinforcement learning, and alignment. Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work. Astra saturates FrontierMath Tier 4 with a 98% score, having already helpedsolve long-standing open problems⁠in mathematics. Astra also saturates ARC-AGI-3 with a 99.9% score and ExploitBench with a 100% score. It also sets a new frontier on computer and browser use, handling the most demanding professional work with unmatched speed, accuracy, and judgment.

GPT‑6 Astra is rolling out today to a limited set of organizations and over the coming days will become available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users, as well as through the OpenAI API, Microsoft Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

Astra is our most aligned model, with substantial improvements in understanding user intent and model behavior—you can delegate tasks with greater confidence in Astra’s judgment. As one way that we test  this, we built a new evaluation informed by the Hugging Face incident that evaluates whether a model facing a difficult or impossible task will go beyond its intended scope. Compared to GPT‑5.6 Sol, which without production safeguards went beyond the authorized target 48% of the time, GPT‑6 Astra did this in 0% of cases.

GPT‑6 Astra marks a new frontier in the speed, accuracy, and safety of computer use. It can take care of tedious tasks like filling out online forms, updating customer records in a CRM, and organizing your calendar. It can conduct online research and draft summaries in your email or in your document editor. It can analyze scientific data, generate plots, create a website, and run frontend QA checks to make sure all the features on that site work. It can help you autonomously install and test software, and troubleshoot problems you see on screen. These improvements are also reflected in our state-of-the-art evaluation results.

These improvements also result in significant efficiency gains in real knowledge-work tasks. In latency simulations on OSWorld 2.0, Astra achieves higher computer-use performance in about 47% less time per task than GPT‑5.6 Sol, scoring 72.6% at roughly 40 minutes per task, compared with 65.7% at roughly 75 minutes.3

GPT‑6 Astra’s computer-use capabilities can be seen in outputs across domains, including game development, electrical engineering, and everyday knowledge work:

Alongside Astra, we are also updating the Codex harness to significantly improve the speed of computer use. Combined with Astra’s efficiency, this translates to a 1.9x faster task completion compared to the current GPT‑5.6 Sol experience, on the Mind2Web benchmark. The model’s improvements on speed mean it can take on many time-consuming life tasks for you, faster than you can.4

GPT‑6 Astra pairs advances in computer use with targeted training for professional environments, to help tackle complex work tasks. It combines the intelligence required for complex problems with the ability to carry out multistep workflows and produce polished documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.

GPT‑6 Astra is our best model for adhering to existing templates and producing slides that are well laid out and succinctly convey key points with a structured narrative. It creates clear, well-structured documents, presentations, spreadsheets, and analyses that follow your templates and match your writing and visual style. Astra is also trained to specifically pull only the context that matters into outputs, instead of repeating information unnecessary for the work at hand. All this means it can output more immediately usable artifacts that match your business context and standards.

GPT‑6Astra also brings stronger visual judgment to the websites, games, applications, and renderings it builds. WithSites⁠(opens in a new window)in ChatGPT, Astra can create, host, and share websites, web apps, and games directly from a prompt.

When instructions leave room for interpretation, GPT‑6 Astra is better than previous models at making the right call. It uses context to fill in routine gaps and asks focused questions when the answer could change the outcome. In Codex, it can ask asynchronously while continuing work that doesn’t depend on your reply. If you don’t respond, it proceeds with sensible assumptions where appropriate, but waits for your input on consequential decisions.

The examples below show how Astra collaborates on everyday tasks where missing information can materially change the answer.

Astra is also better at staying oriented as a task evolves. Earlier models sometimes treated steering messages as a new goal, losing track of the original request or earlier constraints. Astra incorporates new requirements, changes course when asked, and answers side questions without dropping the broader task.

GPT‑6Astra is the best model for software engineering to date.

With Astra, we’re introducing a new way for Codex to preserve and retrieve context when the context window fills. Historically, models have used compaction to summarize work during long sessions, such as when debugging complex issues or tackling large refactors. Each compaction can leave out details about why a fix failed or how a component behaves. In Codex, Astra can keep notes across context windows, preserving accumulated details without repeatedly compressing them into a single summary. Earlier context windows remain searchable, so Astra can find requirements or test results from previous messages and tool outputs—even if that information wasn’t captured in its notes. You can enable this experimental feature in yourCodex config.toml,⁠(opens in a new window)and it will become the default for Astra in the coming weeks.

GPT‑6 Astra is a major advance for scientific discovery, mathematics, and health. Today, we’re sharing two further results on the gaps between prime numbers.9,10

Astra also sets new records across a suite of math and scienceevaluations.

Astra can help with the practical work behind scientific discovery. By combining scientific reasoning with computer use, it can work directly in specialized software to inspect data and explore results, helping researchers assess the evidence and decide what to investigate next.

As we discussed in oursafety update⁠, Astra is a significant jump in cyber capabilities and meets theCritical thresholdin cybersecurity under ourPreparedness Framework. Its ability to identify and develop zero-day exploits can help defenders find and patch weaknesses, but it also creates a need for stronger safeguards. To understand how far these capabilities extend, we ran Astra on internal and third-party expert evaluations.

We first tested the model without production safeguards on ExploitBench and ExploitGym, which evaluate whether models can turn known software vulnerabilities into working exploits. On ExploitBench, Astra achieved a perfect score of 100%, compared with 78.5% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, our previous frontier cyber-capable model. On ExploitGym, Astra reached a 42.4% success rate, compared with 30.3% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, while using substantially fewer output tokens.13

Given concerns that exposure to historical software vulnerabilities may have affected benchmark results, we also evaluated Astra on two novel benchmarks. For one, we built an internal “ExploitBench (June–August 2026)” evaluation to test exploit development using vulnerabilities from the previous three months.14Astra achieved substantially higher arbitrary code-execution rates than GPT‑5.6 Sol on this dataset while using far fewer output tokens. During the evaluation, Astra even discovered and used two previously unknown zero-day vulnerabilities. We are disclosing both vulnerabilities to their maintainers.

We also tested Astra on SRE-Bench15, a benchmark that measures whether models can reverse engineer software binaries to understand its core logic without access to raw source code. Astra solved 88.0% of tasks in a single attempt and 99.2% within four attempts, compared with 55.9% and 68.7% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, respectively.

Beyond benchmarks, expert-led assessments found that Astra, when run without production safeguards, could use previously unknown vulnerabilities to achieve arbitrary code execution in hardened browsers and create privilege-escalation exploits for hardened operating-systems.

As we discussed inThe Defender’s Window, frontier cyber capabilities can help defenders find weaknesses faster, but they also make those weaknesses easier to exploit, raising the urgency for defenders to adapt. With the version of Astra launching today, defenders can use it to complete tasks such as secure code review and patching.

However, Astra will refuse to comply with more advanced cybersecurity tasks such as creating proof-of-concept exploits for vulnerabilities. ThroughOpenAI Daybreak⁠, we plan to expand access and roll out less restrictive safeguards in the coming weeks. This will enable more defensive workflows, including vulnerability and proof-of-concept validation, malware analysis, and detection engineering.

We have also strengthened our protections against potential cyber misuse, building upon our safeguards stack for GPT‑5.6 Sol. These include stronger model robustness to better withstand potential jailbreaks and more context for our monitoring systems. We have continued rigorous internal and external testing, including automated evaluations with ourinternal red-teaming attackers. More details about our cyber safeguards and testingare available in the Astrasafety overview⁠andsystem card⁠(opens in a new window)..

articles.title: Anthropic Launches OSS Scanner, a Free AI Vulnerability Scanner
articles.content: Anthropic has launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in vulnerability scanner for critical open-source projects. The Anthropic OSS Scanner runs the company’s strongest models, including Claude Mythos, against enrolled codebases. Reports go straight to maintainers without human review. That trade delivers faster findings, but shifts triage work onto project teams. 11 days after the October 8 launch, Anthropic reported 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings. TL;DR Scale: 114 projects accepted from about 650 applications, as of October 19. Runs on: Anthropic’s infrastructure, free. Maintainers supply a Dockerfile; audits run in an isolated VM with no Internet. Performance: 85 of 97 audited critical and high findings (88%) met Anthropic’s disclosure bar. Best: Only 1 of 97 audited findings was a false positive. wolfSSL says 72 of 74 reports were valid. Worst: No human review before delivery. 11 of 97 audited findings duplicated known issues; maintainers report inflated severity. What is Anthropic OSS Scanner? OSS Scanner is a free application from Anthropic that periodically audits open-source repositories with its strongest models. The Frontier Red Team and Safeguards Research team run it together. The design borrows from Google’s OSS-Fuzz, but swaps fuzzers for language models. The main goal is a review bottleneck. Over 6 months, Anthropic’s models surfaced over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities. Human reviewers triaged roughly 6,000 of them. Nearly 5,000 more reports went directly to maintainers who asked for everything, validated or not. OSS Scanner turns that ad hoc request into an opt-in program. How does OSS Scanner work? Core maintainers enroll by opening a pull request on anthropics/oss-scanner. The PR adds projects/<project>/project.yaml, based on the project template. Required fields: repo, primary_contact, and a Dockerfile path. Optional fields: threat_model, pgp for encrypted reports, auto_ccs, homepage, and disabled. The Dockerfile builds the project with network access. The VM then moves to a network without Internet for the audit. Agents in the pipeline double-check bugs, run root cause analysis and propose patches. Each report contains a self-contained reproducer and an explanation of the bug. Where possible, it includes a bisection to the commit that introduced it. A candidate patch is attached when available. An optional threat_model.md defines adversarial inputs, out-of-scope code and a severity rubric. Without it, the scanner guesses. How accurate are OSS Scanner reports? Anthropic team asked its penetration testers to check 97 critical and high findings across 48 projects. 85 (88%) met the bar for Anthropic’s coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) process. 11 were real but duplicated known issues or other scan findings. 1 was invalid. Maintainer data points in the same direction. wolfSSL received 74 reports; all but 2 were valid, and 5 became CVEs. curl patched CVE-2026-92392, a High-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free. It affects curl 8.12.0 to 8.22.0 and is fixed in 8.23.0, released October 14, 2026. Anthropic links the timing to benchmark progress. On CyberGym, LLMs went from finding under 20% of vulnerabilities to over 85%. Its broader CVD dashboard lists 6,157 disclosed vulnerabilities across 591 projects, as of October 2. 516 of those are patched. && OSS Scanner vs other open-source security programs FeatureAnthropic OSS ScannerGoogle OSS-FuzzOpenAI Codex for OSSGoogle DeepMind CodeMenderApproachLLM agents (Claude Mythos and others) audit sourceFuzzing: libFuzzer, AFL++, Honggfuzz plus sanitizersCodex Security agent, run by approved maintainersGemini Deep Think agent finds and patches bugsCost to maintainersFree; Anthropic covers full costFreeApproved maintainers get ChatGPT Pro, API credits, conditional Codex Security accessNot disclosedEnrollmentPR with project.yaml and DockerfilePR with project files to google/oss-fuzzApplication, reviewed by OpenAINot disclosed (research project)Human review before maintainer sees itNoNot disclosedMaintainer runs and reviews scansYes, every patch before upstreamReport contentsReproducer, explanation, bisection, candidate patchCrash reports with reproducersFindings with validation and patchesPatches submitted upstreamDisclosure deadlineNone on unvalidated findings90 days or fix release, plus 14-day graceNot disclosedNot disclosedPublished track record77 critical + 803 high model-rated findings in 11 days13,000+ vulnerabilities, 50,000 bugs, 1,000 projects (May 2025)14 CVEs in OSS projects72 security fixes upstreamed (Oct 2025)Precision data88% of 97 audited critical/high validNot disclosedFalse positives cut by 50%+ in betaNot disclosed Sources: OSS-Fuzz disclosure guidelines, OpenAI Codex Security, DeepMind CodeMender. Key Takeaways OSS Scanner gives critical open-source projects free Claude Mythos audits. Reports skip human review; 88% of 97 audited critical/high findings were valid. First 11 days: 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings. Enrollment is a PR with a Dockerfile; audits run offline. No 90-day deadline applies to unvalidated findings. Check out the launch post, the OSS Scanner FAQ and the GitHub repo. Also, feel free to follow us on Twitter and don’t forget to join our 150k+ML SubReddit and Subscribe to our Newsletter. articles.title: Nanbeige Releases Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B Open Agentic Coding Model
articles.content: Nanbeige LLM Lab has released Nanbeige4.3-33B on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. Nanbeige4.3-33B is a 33B dense language model built for agentic coding and office-style ‘cowork’ tasks. The lab sits inside the recruitment platform BOSS Zhipin. It also published Nanbeige4.3-33B-Base for custom post-training. The model supports a 524,288-token context window. In the lab’s own table, it leads 17 of 20 benchmarks against 3 open models near 30B. TL;DR Size: 33B parameters, dense (no MoE), 524,288-token (512K) context, BF16 weights. Runs on: Multi-GPU servers. The card’s SGLang and vLLM recipes use 4-way tensor parallelism. BF16 weights need about 66 GB (our arithmetic). 1 community quantization is listed. Performance: Leads 17 of 20 rows in Nanbeige’s own comparison against Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B and Gemma4-31B. Best: 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, versus 73.0 for Qwen3.8-27B. Worst: 23.8 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (its lowest score). It also trails Qwen3.8-27B on SWE-Bench Pro, 60.3 vs 61.7. What is Nanbeige4.3-33B? Nanbeige4.3-33B is the flagship ‘teacher’ model of the Nanbeige4.3 series. The lab’s stated strategy is to build a strong teacher first. It then plans to distill agentic skills into smaller models, starting with Nanbeige4.3-3B. How is Nanbeige4.3-33B built? The config.json declares a standard LlamaForCausalLM architecture. There is no expert routing, so all 33B parameters run on every token. 52 layers, hidden size 7,168 56 query heads and 8 key-value heads (grouped-query attention), head dimension 128 FFN intermediate size 22,016, vocabulary of 166,912 tokens RoPE theta of 120,000,000 and 524,288 max positions The chat template exposes 3 controls. enable_thinking toggles reasoning and is on by default. preserve_thinking keeps reasoning from earlier turns. Nanbeige recommends it for multi-turn tool use and code agents. Passing tools enables tool calling, and an XML call format is recommended. How does Nanbeige4.3-33B perform on benchmarks? Nanbeige compared the model with Qwen3.8-27B, Muse-Glimmer-30B and Gemma4-31B. Every model ran at its highest thinking effort, with shared hyperparameters and harnesses. All scores in this section are self-reported. Agentic coding: It scores 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, against 73.0 for Qwen3.8-27B. DeepSWE shows the widest gap: 65.5 versus 42.5. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, it scores 23.8 while Gemma4-31B scores 0.0. Agentic cowork: It posts 54.2 on Automation Bench versus 38.3, and 44.8 on JobBench versus 34.5. On YC-bench, simulated earnings reach $1,025,437 versus $641,290. Reasoning: It reports 95.2 on AIME 2026 and 84.0 on AA-LCR. It loses 3 of 20 rows. Qwen3.8-27B leads SWE-Bench Pro (61.7 vs 60.3) and GDPval (86.4 vs 84.8). Gemma4-31B leads GPQA Diamond in Nanbeige’s table, 91.3 vs 89.5. The Base model beats Gemma4-31B-Base on all 8 reported tasks. Examples include MMLU-Pro (66.9 vs 59.3) and GPQA (62.0 vs 41.5). articles.title: Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time
articles.content: Hugging Face has released Carbon-X, an open DNA language model with 14.8B parameters. Carbon-X is a decoder-only model from Hugging Face Bio. It reads raw DNA in a chat and answers in English. It predicts whether mutations are benign or pathogenic, flags regulatory regions, classifies organisms and predicts next bases. The weights ship under Apache 2.0, so labs can keep sensitive sequences on their own GPUs. Hugging Face built it with Zhongguancun Academy and TIGEM / University of Naples Federico II. TL;DR Size: 14.8B parameters (dense, no MoE), 40,960-token context. Runs on: 1 x 80 GB GPU in bfloat16 via vLLM or Transformers. Official GGUF: Q8_0 is 15.8 GB, Q4_K_M is 9.6 GB. Performance: 66.7% average on 5 DNA benchmarks, best of every open model tested (self-reported). Best: 74.9% on BioReason Coding, ahead of every model tested, open or closed. Worst: 29.8% on GenomeQA splice-site questions. What is Carbon-X and how does it work? Carbon-X starts from Qwen3-14B. DNA and text share 1 token stream in 1 decoder. There is no separate DNA encoder, unlike earlier work such as BioReason. The key structure piece is a hybrid tokenizer. It keeps Qwen3’s BPE vocabulary for text and adds 5,515 DNA tokens. These include 4,096 non-overlapping 6-mers, 1,364 tail tokens and 3 markers. One DNA token covers 6 base pairs. DNA runs of 6 or more A/C/G/T bases are tagged automatically. The backbone is a standard Qwen3 stack. It has 40 layers, hidden size 5120 and GQA with 8 KV heads. How was Carbon-X trained? Training ran in four stages, per the model card: Embedding warmup: about 10B tokens with the transformer frozen, so only the new DNA embeddings learn. Mid-training: 302B tokens at 8,192 sequence length. The mix is 55% raw DNA, 20% English, 15% biology text and 10% instruction data. articles.summary: Hugging Face Bio가 DNA 서열을 입력받아 영어로 답하는 148억 매개변수 공개 모델 Carbon-X를 선보였다. Qwen3-14B에 DNA 전용 토큰을 추가해 별도 DNA 인코더 없이 자연어와 서열을 하나의 디코더에서 처리하며, 변이 병원성 예측과 조절 영역 탐지 등을 지원한다. 자체 평가에서 DNA 벤치마크 5종 평균 66.7%를 기록했지만, GenomeQA의 스플라이스 부위 문항에서는 29.8%에 그쳐 과제별 편차가 컸다. Apache 2.0 가중치를 자체 GPU에 배포할 수 있어 민감한 서열의 외부 전송을 피할 수 있지만, 제시된 결과만으로 임상적 유효성이 입증된 것은 아니다.

articles.title: “모르면 추측 대신 기억을 확인한다”…ETRI·GIST, 스스로 판단하고 행동하는 로봇 AI 플랫폼 공개
articles.content:
로봇이 주변 환경을 직접 관찰하고, 과거에 확인한 정보를 기억에서 찾아 검증한 뒤 행동하는 새로운 인공지능(AI) 기술이 개발됐다. 기존 로봇 AI가 불확실한 상황에서 언어모델의 사전 지식에 의존해 잘못 판단하는 문제를 줄이고, 실제 관측한 사실을 바탕으로 복잡한 작업을 수행하도록 하는 기술이다.

한국전자통신연구원(ETRI)은 광주과학기술원(GIST)과 공동으로 환경 관측과 능동적 기억 검색을 결합한 로봇 AI 에이전트 '씬쿼리플래너(SceneQueryPlanner)'를 개발했다고 26일 밝혔다.

연구진은 로봇이 공간과 사물의 위치, 재질, 상태 등을 구조화된 기억으로 저장하고, 작업 수행 과정에서 필요한 정보를 스스로 검색하거나 추가 관측하도록 설계했다. 이를 통해 기존 방식 대비 복합작업 성공률을 최대 24%포인트 높였다.

로봇 AI의 새로운 과제...'무엇을 할까'보다 '무엇을 확인할까'

최근 대형언어모델(LLM)의 발전으로 로봇은 사람의 자연어 명령을 이해하고 여러 단계의 행동을 계획할 수 있게 됐다. 그러나 실제 생활환경에서는 언어를 이해하는 것만으로 작업을 정확하게 수행하기 어렵다. 물체의 위치와 종류뿐 아니라 재질, 현재 상태, 주변 사물과의 관계 등 세부적인 환경정보를 파악해야 하기 때문이다.

예를 들어 사용자가 "식탁 위 유리컵은 선반에, 플라스틱 컵은 캐비닛에 정리해 줘"라고 지시하면 로봇은 컵을 찾는 것에서 그치지 않고 각각의 재질을 구분해야 한다. 또 "켜져 있는 전자제품을 모두 꺼줘"라는 명령을 수행하려면 어떤 전자제품이 있는지, 현재 전원이 켜져 있는지 확인해야 한다.

기존 대형언어모델 기반 로봇 에이전트는 주변 환경을 관측한 정보를 긴 문장 형태로 전달받아 행동을 계획하는 경우가 많았다. 하지만 관측정보가 부족하면 물체의 속성을 잘못 추측할 수 있고, 반대로 정보가 지나치게 많으면 작업과 관계없는 내용까지 처리해야 해 추론의 안정성이 떨어질 수 있다.

연구진은 이러한 문제를 '수동적 관측(Passive Observation)'에 따른 한계로 설명했다. 필요한 정보가 누락되거나 불필요한 정보가 과도하게 제공되는 환경에서는 AI가 잘못된 근거로 판단하는 환각(Hallucination)과 불안정한 추론이 발생할 수 있다는 것이다.

이를 해결하기 위해 연구진은 로봇이 정보를 수동적으로 전달받는 방식에서 벗어나, 현재 작업에 필요한 정보가 무엇인지 판단하고 직접 확보하는 능동적 정보 탐색(Active Information Seeking) 방식을 제안했다.

3차원 장면 그래프에 공간·사물·상태 저장...로봇의 구조화된 기억 구현

씬쿼리플래너의 핵심 기술은 로봇이 관측한 환경정보를 '3차원 장면 그래프(3D Scene Graph)'로 구성해 저장하는 것이다. 3차원 장면 그래프는 공간을 방과 가구, 물체 등으로 구분하고 각각의 위치와 속성, 상호 관계를 연결한 구조화된 정보 표현 방식이다.

예를 들어 거실에 있는 탁자와 탁자 위 컵, 주방의 캐비닛과 선반 등을 각각의 객체로 표현하고, 물체가 어디에 놓여 있는지와 어떤 속성을 갖는지를 관계 정보로 연결한다.

물체의 재질뿐 아니라 문이 열려 있는지, 전자제품의 전원이 켜져 있는지 등 작업에 필요한 상태 정보도 저장할 수 있다. 이러한 기억은 새로운 관측정보가 들어오면 갱신된다. 로봇이 다른 방으로 이동한 뒤에도 이전에 관측한 환경정보를 활용할 수 있도록 설계된 것이다.

특히 씬쿼리플래너는 저장된 모든 정보를 한꺼번에 언어모델에 제공하지 않는다. 현재 수행해야 할 작업과 직접 관련된 정보만 선택적으로 검색한다. 이를 통해 환경정보가 증가하더라도 불필요한 내용이 추론 과정에 개입하는 문제를 줄이고, 여러 공간에 걸친 장기 작업에서도 필요한 정보를 활용하도록 했다.

환경 관측과 기억 검색 결합...정보 확인 자체를 행동 계획에 포함

연구진이 제안한 핵심 개념은 '기억·환경 이중 그라운딩(Memory–Environment Dual-Grounding)'이다. 그라운딩은 AI의 판단과 추론을 실제 관측정보나 확인 가능한 데이터에 연결하는 과정을 의미한다.

씬쿼리플래너는 두 가지 정보 확인 방식을 결합한다. 먼저 '환경 그라운딩(Environment Grounding)'은 로봇이 직접 주변을 관찰하거나 이동하면서 필요한 정보를 확보하는 방식이다. 반면 '메모리 그라운딩(Memory Grounding)'은 이전에 관측해 저장한 기억에서 현재 작업에 필요한 정보를 검색하는 방식이다.

씬쿼리플래너는 사용자의 명령을 세부 작업으로 나누고, 각 단계에서 필요한 정보가 무엇인지 판단한다. 이후 저장된 기억을 검색할지, 주변 환경을 추가로 관측할지 선택한다.

연구진은 정보 획득 자체를 행동 계획의 핵심 요소로 취급했다. 즉, 로봇이 물체를 집거나 이동하는 동작뿐 아니라 '어떤 정보를 확인해야 하는가'까지 계획하도록 한 것이다. 예를 들어 컵을 재질별로 분류해야 한다면 로봇은 먼저 컵의 위치를 파악하고, 기억에 저장된 재질 정보를 조회한다. 필요한 정보가 부족하면 추가적인 환경 관측을 통해 확인한 뒤 물체를 이동한다.

이처럼 추측에 의존하지 않고 필요한 정보를 명시적으로 확인하는 구조는 여러 단계에 걸친 복잡한 작업에서 판단 오류를 줄이는 데 도움이 된다.

새로운 평가체계 '앳플랜-벤치' 개발...복합작업 수행 능력 검증

연구진은 기술의 효과를 검증하기 위해 속성 기반 행동 계획 평가체계인 '앳플랜-벤치(AttPlan-Bench)'도 개발했다. 앳플랜-벤치는 여러 방으로 구성된 가정환경에서 장기간에 걸쳐 수행해야 하는 복합작업을 평가하도록 설계됐다.

평가에는 물체 이동과 정리, 가열과 냉각, 청소, 전자제품의 전원 조작 등 10가지 유형의 작업이 포함됐다. 특히 단순히 물체를 찾아 이동하는 작업을 넘어 재질이나 상태, 위치관계를 정확하게 확인해야 하는 속성 기반 작업을 포함했다. 이는 AI가 일반적인 행동 계획을 생성하는 능력뿐 아니라, 실제 환경에서 확보한 정보를 바탕으로 판단하는 능력을 평가하기 위한 것이다.

연구진은 기존의 추론·행동 결합 방식인 '리액트(ReAct)'와 씬쿼리플래너의 성능을 비교했다. 리액트는 언어모델이 추론과 행동을 반복하면서 문제를 해결하는 대표적인 AI 에이전트 접근법이다. 그러나 환경정보를 수동적으로 전달받는 구조에서는 필요한 세부 정보가 누락되거나 불필요한 정보가 누적되는 한계가 있다.

씬쿼리플래너는 이 과정에 선택적인 기억 검색과 환경 관측을 추가해 작업 수행에 필요한 정보를 확보하도록 했다.

라마 3.1 성공률 69.6%, 큐웬 2.5는 68.0%...최대 24%p 개선

실험 결과 씬쿼리플래너는 오픈소스와 상용 언어모델을 활용한 평가에서 기존 리액트 방식보다 높은 작업 성공률을 기록했다. 메타(Meta)의 라마 3.1(LLaMA 3.1)을 활용한 실험에서는 작업 성공률이 기존 46.8%에서 69.6%로 상승했다. 이는 22.8%포인트 개선된 수치다.

알리바바의 큐웬 2.5(Qwen 2.5)를 적용한 실험에서는 기존 44.0%에서 68.0%로 높아져 24.0%포인트 향상됐다. 오픈AI의 GPT-4o를 활용한 실험에서도 모든 평가환경에서 기존 방식보다 높은 성능을 나타냈다. 특히 물체의 속성을 확인해야 하는 복합작업의 성공률은 17.2%포인트 개선됐다.

이번 결과는 언어모델의 규모를 확대하거나 새로운 모델을 학습시키는 것 외에도, 환경정보를 검색하고 검증하는 에이전트 구조를 개선하는 방식으로 작업 수행 능력을 높일 수 있음을 보여준다.

특히 연구진은 논문에서 기억과 환경을 결합한 이중 그라운딩 방식이 다양한 작업에서 보다 안정적이고 확장성 있는 추론을 지원한다고 설명했다. 다만 이러한 성능은 연구진이 구축한 벤치마크 환경에서 확인된 결과다. 실제 가정이나 산업현장에서 로봇이 동일한 성공률을 보인다는 의미는 아니다.

피지컬 AI의 핵심 기술로 주목, 실제 로봇 환경으로 확대 추진

이번 연구는 로봇 AI의 성능을 높이기 위해 더 많은 정보를 기억시키는 것보다, 필요한 정보를 정확한 시점에 검색하고 확인하도록 하는 것이 중요하다는 점을 제시했다. 이는 가정용 로봇뿐 아니라 돌봄·서비스 로봇, 산업현장의 자율작업 로봇 등 다양한 피지컬 AI(Physical AI) 분야로 확장될 가능성이 있다.

특히 실제 환경에서는 물체의 위치와 상태가 지속적으로 바뀌기 때문에 로봇이 과거의 기억과 현재 관측정보를 비교하면서 행동을 계획하는 능력이 중요하다.

ETRI 소셜로보틱스연구실 최재우 선임연구원(과학기술연합대학원대학교, UST 인공지능 전공 조교수)은 "이번 기술은 로봇이 관측한 환경정보를 체계적으로 기억하고, 필요한 순간에 스스로 찾아 활용하도록 한 것이 핵심"이라며 "앞으로 실제 생활환경에서도 로봇이 불확실한 정보를 추측하기보다 자신의 경험과 기억을 확인하며 안정적으로 행동하도록 기술을 고도화하겠다"고 말했다.

GIST 김의환 교수는 "3차원 장면 그래프는 로봇이 관측한 공간을 방·가구·물체의 계층과 관계로 정리한 구조화된 기억"이라며 "이번 연구는 이 기억을 단순히 저장하는 데 그치지 않고, 에이전트가 필요한 정보를 스스로 질의해 꺼내 쓰는 능동적 메모리로 발전시켰다는 데 의미가 있다"고 설명했다.

연구진은 씬쿼리플래너와 앳플랜-벤치의 코드 및 평가 도구를 공개해 후속 연구에 활용할 수 있도록 했다. 향후에는 카메라와 센서에서 수집되는 불완전한 정보와 실제 환경의 변화에 대응할 수 있도록 기술을 확장할 계획이다.

이번 연구는 AI가 언어를 이해하고 행동을 계획하는 단계를 넘어, 자신의 판단에 필요한 근거를 능동적으로 확인하는 방향으로 발전하고 있음을 보여준다.

특히 로봇이 잘못된 추측에 따라 행동할 경우 물체 파손이나 안전사고로 이어질 수 있다는 점에서, 기억 검색과 환경 검증을 결합한 접근법은 차세대 피지컬 AI의 신뢰성과 자율성을 높이는 중요한 연구 방향으로 평가된다.

한편, 이번 연구는 최재우 ETRI 선임연구원과 오세훈, 김의환 GIST 교수 등이 참여했으며, 지난 24일부터 29일까지 헝가리 부다페스트에서 열리는 EMNLP 2026에서 '체화형 AI 에이전트를 위한 기억·환경 이중 그라운딩: 수동적 관측을 넘어선 능동적 정보 탐색(Memory–Environment Dual-Grounding for Embodied Agents: Active Information Seeking Beyond Passive Observation-다운)'란 제목로  지난 25일 발표됐다.

현재, 연구진은 씬쿼리플래너의 소스코드와 복합작업 평가 벤치마크인 앳플랜-벤치를 깃허브(GitHub-다운)를 통해 공개했으며, 개발자들은 이를 활용해 새로운 로봇 AI 에이전트를 개발하고 기존 기술과 성능을 비교·검증할 수 있다.
articles.summary: ETRI와 GIST가 환경 관측과 능동적 기억 검색을 결합한 로봇 AI 에이전트 씬쿼리플래너를 개발했다. 공간과 사물의 위치·재질·상태를 3차원 장면 그래프로 저장하고, 작업에 필요한 정보만 검색하거나 추가 관측하도록 계획한다. 연구진은 언어모델의 사전 지식에 기대어 추측하는 문제를 줄여 기존 방식 대비 복합작업 성공률을 최대 24%포인트 높였다고 밝혔다. 여러 방을 오가며 물건을 정리하거나 기기의 상태를 확인하는 작업에 활용할 수 있는 접근이지만, 제공된 자료에는 성능 개선의 세부 평가 조건이 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents
articles.content: Microsoft Research has open-sourced Agensh, a decentralized harness for large teams of coding agents. The Agensh multi-agent harness removes the central orchestrator that most agent frameworks depend on. Every worker picks its own sub-task, shares findings and merges code into a common Git repo. On ProgramBench, the team scaled the setup from 1 agent to 1,024 agents. TL;DR A Harness: Tested from 1 to 1,024 agents. Each worker gets a 272,000-token input and 128,000-token output limit. Runs on: Linux with Docker Compose. Single node by default (8 workers). The 1,024-agent run used 16 nodes, 64 agents each. Workers have a 64 GiB memory ceiling. Performance: more agents raised scores on all 5 hardest ProgramBench tasks, and reached them sooner. Best: 79.59% pandoc pass rate with 32 agents on GPT-6.1-sol. GPT-5.6-sol hit 55.06% with 1,024 agents. Worst: the 5-task mean reached only 28.78% at 128 agents. Going from 1 to 8 agents added 1.37 points. What is Agensh? Agensh is a multi-agent harness from Microsoft Research that coordinates many LLM agents without a lead agent. The target problem is the orchestrator ceiling. In orchestrator-worker designs, a lead agent plans, assigns and merges all work. The research paper cites Claude Code agent teams, Codex sub-agents, Copilot fleet and Kimi Agent Swarm as examples. Agensh lets the workers do that coordination themselves. How does the Agensh cooperation loop work? Each worker runs the same 5-step loop, concurrently and asynchronously: Gather context: read the goal, peer progress, messages and findings. Claim a sub-task: post a CLAIM, then settle overlaps by direct message. Take action: work locally with tools and post useful findings early. Verify results: check the work against the sub-task’s acceptance criteria. Merge progress: merge into the shared repo, post an update, then repeat. Three services connect the workers. Gitea hosts the shared workspace, with branches, PRs and merge conflicts. Mattermost carries a team channel plus direct messages for urgent collisions. A shared context board, adapted from DeLM, stores typed notes: OBSERVED, FACT, FAIL, CLAIM and PATCH_SUMMARY. The loop lives in the prompt, not in runtime code. Every worker gets the same prompt except its ID. Agensh sits on top of a single-agent harness. The experiments used GitHub Copilot CLI. The research paper states thin adapters can connect other harnesses, such as Claude Code. &&& How well does Agensh scale on ProgramBench? Microsoft team tested the 5 hardest ProgramBench tasks: FFmpeg, gromacs, pandoc, PHP-src and ctags. Agents rebuild each program from its observed behavior. They work offline, within 6 hours. Reference repos range from 2,767 files (pandoc) to 26,266 files (PHP-src). With GPT-5.6-sol at high reasoning effort, the mean final test-pass rate moved as follows: 1 agent: 19.31% 8 agents: 20.68% 32 agents: 26.52% 128 agents: 28.78% That is a 9.47-point gain, about 49% relative. On pandoc alone, scores were 33.89% (1), 41.75% (8), 43.11% (32), 50.94% (128) and 55.06% (1,024). Speed improved too: on pandoc, 128 agents passed 30% at the 30-minute checkpoint. 32 and 8 agents needed 60 and 90 minutes. The README adds a newer model. With GPT-6.1-sol, pandoc rose from 56.19% (1 agent) to 79.59% (32 agents). That is a 41.64% relative gain. These GPT-6.1-sol figures are not in the v1 paper. What behaviors emerged as the team grew? The research team traced worker trajectories at each scale: 8 agents: peers agreed on interfaces and resolved overlapping claims themselves. 32 agents: peers reviewed shared work; one approval was withdrawn after a counterexample. 128 agents: workers reused trusted reviewers and standardized an integration protocol. 1,024 agents: several workers acted as integrators, and peers recovered failed work. None of these roles was hard-coded. How does Agensh compare with other multi-agent harnesses? The release includes a single-node Docker Compose team and a single-agent baseline. Both use native Copilot ACP sessions. You need Linux with Docker Engine, Compose v2, systemd, cgroup v2 and Python 3.11+. Defaults are 8 workers, 6 hours per task and gpt-5.6-sol at high effort. You also need ProgramBench (v1.2.5 was validated) and a model API token. Full steps sit in the reproduction guide. Key Takeaways Agensh coordinates up to 1,024 agents with no central orchestrator. Workers self-claim tasks via Gitea, Mattermost and a shared findings board. 128 agents lifted the 5-task ProgramBench mean from 19.31% to 28.78%. GPT-6.1-sol with 32 agents hit 79.59% on pandoc. Code is MIT licensed, but token cost is not disclosed. Check out the Paper, GitHub Repo and Project Page. articles.title: Researchers from Stanford and UC Berkeley Introduce TokenGate: Token-Gated Attention Makes Long-Context Prefill Up to 11.3x Faster
articles.content: Stanford and UC Berkeley researchers released TokenGate, a module for long-context prefill. TokenGate learned token pruning lets an existing LLM skim its input. Only the tokens that matter get full processing. The research team reports 1.4x to 11.3x faster time-to-first-token (TTFT) with no accuracy loss. Peak prefill memory drops 1.5x to 3.4x. Code and checkpoints are on GitHub under Apache-2.0. TL;DR MLP gate: A small MLP gate and LoRA (r=16) added to Qwen3-1.7B or Qwen3.5-2B. Tested on contexts up to 128k tokens. Runs on: Paper timings use 1 A100 at batch size 1. Training used 4 A100s. Performance: Pareto-optimal on 5 tasks against 6 baselines. Best: NIAH 16k at 11.3x faster TTFT and 3.42x lower memory. TTFT gain hits 13.0x at 128k. Worst: Speedup drops to 1.4x on some tasks. What is TokenGate? TokenGate is a drop-in component that adds trainable token pruning to pretrained LLMs. Transformers push every token through every layer. Attention cost grows quadratically with length. Training-free pruning is cheap but loses accuracy at high pruning rates. Architectural changes often need pre-training from scratch. How does TokenGate learned token pruning work? The forward pass splits into 3 phases: Standard forward: layers below gate layer L process all N tokens as usual. Gate module: an MLP scores each token from its post-attention residual at layer L. A top-K selector keeps the highest-scoring tokens. Pruned forward: layers above L process only those K tokens and never create KV entries for pruned ones. Only the document part of the prompt is prunable. The question is never pruned. What is token-gated attention? Top-K selection is not differentiable, which blocks end-to-end training. TokenGate borrows the Mixture-of-Experts router trick. Each kept token’s score becomes a bias on attention logits above the gate. That bias gives gradients a path back to the scorer. A learnable per-head gain and a learnable temperature refine this. The temperature corrects for each query seeing fewer keys. Training uses plain next-token loss. Each step averages a full-context loss and a random-budget loss. So 1 trained gate works across budgets. && How does TokenGate perform on benchmarks? The research team tested Qwen3-1.7B on RepoBench-P, 2WikiMultihopQA, MultiNews, BioDEX and needle-in-a-haystack (NIAH). Baselines were FastKV, SlimInfer, DASH, GemFilter, FlexPrefill and MInference, on the same LoRA backbone. Versus full prefill: 1.4x to 11.3x faster TTFT and 1.5x to 3.4x lower memory. Versus the next-best baseline: 1.2x to 6.4x faster TTFT and up to 2.1x lower memory. 2WikiMultihopQA: at 95% of full-context accuracy, prefill runs 3.0x faster with 2.7x less memory. Longer contexts: a gate trained at 16k reaches 12.8x at 32k and 13.0x at 64k and 128k. Memory savings stay near 3.43x. The learned selector beats FastKV’s heuristic at the same layer. Even random-K selection scores higher on the TokenGate backbone. The research team credits backbone co-adaptation. Does it work on hybrid-attention models? Yes, Qwen3.5-2B mixes Gated DeltaNet and full-attention layers. On NIAH 32k, TokenGate at layer 3 matched full-prefill accuracy. It ran 3.8x faster than full prefill and 2.1x faster than FastKV. Gating at layers 1 or 2 reached 7.8x, within 6% accuracy. FastKV can only prune attention layers. Pruning layers come from TokenGate’s Appendix C.2. How do you deploy TokenGate? The GitHub Repo needs Python 3.10+ and CUDA PyTorch 2.9+. An optional FlashAttention-2 key-bias kernel speeds up dense Qwen3. It costs 1.0x to 1.1x a plain call. Without it, inference falls back to FlexAttention. A {state} placeholder marks the prunable document. generate takes a max_kept_prefill_tokens budget. Checkpoints cover all 5 tasks on Qwen3-1.7B, plus a Qwen3.5-2B NIAH gate. Example: liana313/tokengate-niah-qwen3-1.7b. Training mirrors a TRL/PEFT recipe. Each step is 1.3x slower than plain LoRA. Runs converged faster on 4 of 5 tasks. Mean training time was 1.8 versus 2.2 A100 hours. Key Takeaways TokenGate adds learned token pruning to existing LLMs via a small gate and LoRA. Prefill runs 1.4x to 11.3x faster with 1.5x to 3.4x lower peak memory. Token-gated attention makes top-K selection trainable, MoE-router style. It beats the next-best pruning baseline by up to 6.4x on TTFT. It works on hybrid Qwen3.5-2B, where FastKV cannot prune DeltaNet layers. Check out the Paper, GitHub repo and Hugging Face paper page. articles.title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
articles.content: Cognition has released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin, a free, open-source set of agent skills. It targets three critical remote code execution (RCE) advisories. They cover PHP2Shell, the Node.js October 21, 2026 security release and a CVSS 10.0 self-managed GitLab bug. The skills run in Devin and in any coding agent that reads SKILL.md files. Cognition packaged the remediation workflow it used internally. Developers can do inventory, approve, patch, test, then ship 1 pull request per repository. TL;DR Size: Three skills (fix-php-vuln, fix-node-vuln, fix-gitlab-vuln), MIT license. Runs on: Devin, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Factory Droid, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode and Windsurf. Needs git, a shell, Docker and registry access. The npx skills install needs Node.js 22.20 or later. Performance: No remediation benchmark or fix-rate number is published for the plugin. Best: Covers the week’s most severe bug, GitLab CVE-2026-110264, rated CVSS 10.0. Worst: Validation is only as strong as your tests. Managed runtimes, appliances and Electron apps are flagged, not patched. What is the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin? The Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin is a set of three Agent Skills from Cognition. They find and patch vulnerable PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments. The source is on GitHub under the MIT license. Cognition’s product page lists it as free and open source. Which vulnerabilities does it fix? PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619): PHP rates both flaws CVSS v4.0 9.2. The first corrupts memory after an out-of-memory condition. The second lets stale global state from one request reach the next. PHP says every web-serving setup is at risk, with mod_php rated highest risk. Fixed versions are 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. PHP 8.1 and older get no releases, only source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. Node.js October 2026 release: It fixes 10 CVEs, 4 rated High. The lead bug, CVE-2026-111497, is a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can enable RCE. Fixed versions are 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1. Node.js 20 and older are end-of-life and get no fix. GitLab CVE-2026-110264: An integer overflow in the regular expression compiler allows unauthenticated code execution. It affects GitLab CE/EE from 7.0 onward and scores CVSS 10.0. GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched. How does the plugin work? Every skill follows the same five-step shape: Read-only inventory: The agent scans Dockerfiles, base images, distro packages, CI, Helm, Terraform, Packer, Lambda and config management. Approval gate: Nothing changes until you pick repos. Riskier minor or major upgrades are called out first. Verified target: Every tag, digest, package version and checksum is confirmed against the official source before editing. Test before and after: The suite runs on the current version, then inside the new production image. Regressions stop the run.
